Files that do not belong in the repository

We left out 14 files that software creates by itself, not the authors: operating system (14). They hold nothing a reader can use, but they clutter the repository, and software can mistake them for real files (for example a ._ copy of a .csv for data).

Remove these: Operating system files: macOS adds a __MACOSX folder and a ._ copy of every file it puts in a zip, and .DS_Store files to folders; Windows adds Thumbs.db and desktop.ini. On a Mac, create zips from the command line with zip -r -X, or remove them afterwards with zip -d archive.zip "__MACOSX/*" "*.DS_Store". RStudio session files (.Rproj.user/) hold open tabs and unsaved edits; R history (.Rhistory, .Rapp.history) lists the commands typed in a session and can hold file paths and passwords; Jupyter checkpoints (.ipynb_checkpoints/) are automatic copies of notebooks; compiled Python files (__pycache__/, .pyc) are recreated when the code runs; open-document lock files (~$...docx, .~lock...#) are left while a document is open; editor backups (file~, .bak, .swp) and temporary files (.tmp, .temp, an interrupted save of R’s workspace, .RDataTmp) are copies a program made by itself.

Keep only on purpose: version control folders (.git, .svn, .hg) hold the project’s history, which can include earlier versions of files and data that was later removed; editor settings (.idea, .vscode) can hold paths on your own computer. A .gitignore based on GitHub’s templates (https://github.com/github/gitignore) keeps them out of a repository.

To check Non-Significant P Value Check

What we found

We found 16 non-significant p values that should be checked for appropriate interpretation.

Show details

Meta-scientific research has shown nonsignificant p values are commonly misinterpreted. It is incorrect to infer that there is ‘no effect’, ‘no difference’, or that groups are ‘the same’ after p > 0.05.

It is possible that there is a true non-zero effect, but that the study did not detect it. Make sure your inference acknowledges that it is possible that there is a non-zero effect. It is correct to include the effect is ‘not significantly’ different, although this just restates that p > 0.05.

Metacheck does not yet analyze automatically whether sentences which include non-significant p-values are correct, but we recommend manually checking the sentences below for possible misinterpreted non-significant p values.

For educational material on preventing the misinterpretation of p values, see Improving Your Statistical Inferences.

Code Comments

Best programming practice is to add comments to code, to explain what the code does (to yourself in the future, or peers who want to re-use your code). All your code files had comments.

Missing Files

All files loaded in the code were present in the repository.

Absolute Paths

Best programming practice is to use relative file paths (e.g., ‘./files’) instead of absolute file paths (e.g., ‘C://Lakens/project_dir/files’) as these folder names do not exist on other computers. No absolute file paths were found in any of the code files.

Working Directory (setwd)

Best programming practice is to avoid setwd() in analysis code: it hardcodes an assumption about the working directory (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine), so the code breaks when run anywhere else. Keep the working directory as the caller sets it and use relative paths. No setwd() calls were found in any of the code files.

Package Installation (install.packages)

Best programming practice is to avoid install.packages() in analysis code: it installs software on whoever runs the script without asking, which is at minimum disruptive (an unexpected install, network access, a package version the author never tested against) and at worst a security risk if it points at an untrusted repository. Document required packages instead (a README, or a list of them: an renv.lock/DESCRIPTION for R, a requirements.txt for Python). No install.packages() calls were found in any of the code files.

Libraries / Imports

Best programming practice is to load all required libraries/imports in one block near the top of the code. In 10 code files, libraries/imports were at multiple places (i.e., with more than 3 non-comment lines in between).

This module runs automated data-quality checks (empty columns, SPSS filter variables, category casing, stray whitespace, numbers stored as text, problematic and colliding column names, mixed text encodings, personal information, spreadsheet formatting, and careless responding) on the extracted data files.

We examined 812 columns across 56 data files.

Issues Identified

108 file/column combinations have at least one issue.

About the personal-information flags. These are pattern matches, not confirmed disclosures, and they are tuned to over-report rather than miss something. Expect false positives:

  • Column names are matched against identifying words in English and other European languages (email, telefoonnummer, geboortedatum, …). A column called phone_number flags whether or not it holds one, and an empty or already-anonymised column flags on its name alone.
  • Values are matched against the shape of an identifier. An IP address pattern also matches a version string or a dotted numeric code; a card-number pattern requires both a real issuer prefix and a checksum, but a long numeric ID can still coincide.
  • Free text is flagged when a column holds long, mostly-distinct prose — the shape open-ended answers take. Most such columns contain no names at all.

A flag means look at this column. Where the data is already de-identified (an ip column reading Anonymized, a name column the authors emptied), no action is needed.

Spreadsheet formatting such as colour, merged cells, and blank rows/columns is not preserved when data are read programmatically or exported to CSV. Store data as a plain rectangular table (one header row, one column per variable, no colour-encoded meaning) so it is machine-readable.

Careless Responding

No file could be screened for careless responding.

What this does not cover. Only 0 of 56 data files could be screened: the rest had no detectable multi-item scale block, or too few respondents. Even in a screened file, these checks only look at multi-item rating scales — the only place where a repeated or flat answer pattern is interpretable. Single questions, open text, demographics and any item outside a detected scale block are never examined. A respondent can therefore answer most of a survey carelessly and still not be flagged here, and finding nothing is not evidence that a dataset is free of careless responding.

Reproducibility Check

We ran the paper’s 2 R scripts and 4 Python scripts in the order they depend on each other, each in an isolated container, for at most 5 minutes per script. Metacheck detected version information that can be used to install specific versions of software for the reproducibility run. We recommend retrying the reproducibility check with recorded_versions = TRUE. This will install the required R packages, if still available. As this takes a long time, this setting is not implemented on this shared server. 6 identical copies of these scripts, which other links in the paper lead to, were not run again.

2 of 6 scripts ran to the end: 1 did not reproduce, 1 could not run because a package or program was not available, and 2 did not finish within our time limit.

Script Result What happened
main_analyses.Rmd Stopped with an error Error in profile.merMod(object, which = parm, signames = signames, …) : Profiling over both the residual variance and fixed effects is not numerically consistent with profiling over the fixed effects only (relative difference: 3.691e-05); consider adjusting devmatchtol
open_ended_labeling.ipynb Ran to the end
prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd Ran to the end
prompt_optimization_LLM_calls.ipynb Ran out of time It was still running after 300 seconds, our time limit per script.
speech_to_text_conversion.ipynb Could not run on our server It needs the Python package whisperx, which we could not install. This is not an error in the script.
chunking_and_scoring_LLM_calls.ipynb Ran out of time It was still running after 300 seconds, our time limit per script.

How to make your code run on another computer

We ran your code on a clean computer, the way a reader or reviewer would. Below is each problem we found, the scripts it affects, and how to fix it. Fix them in the order given: a problem near the top can cause the ones below it.

A package could not be installed.

  • speech_to_text_conversion.ipynb needs whisperx.

whisperx could not be installed with pip. List it with its version in requirements.txt. If it is not on PyPI, or its name there differs from the name the code imports, say in the README how to install it.

A script runs longer than our limit of 5 minutes.

  • prompt_optimization_LLM_calls.ipynb
  • chunking_and_scoring_LLM_calls.ipynb

State in the README how long each script runs. If some steps take hours, save their results (such as fitted models) to files, add those to the deposit, and let the script read them, so readers can check the rest without waiting.

Metacheck can’t automatically establish what caused the error, or how it should be improved.

  • main_analyses.Rmd

Other problems in the files

  • open_ended_labeling.ipynb calls os.chdir(), which sets the folder the script runs in. We replaced the call with one that does nothing, so the script ran from the top folder of the project. All details of the Reproducibility Check

This module assesses whether the paper’s code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 2 R code files.

Run order

No ordering signal (no data dependency, source() call, or numeric filename prefix) distinguishes the run order of these files. They may need to run in a specific order that could not be determined automatically — check this before running.

Order File Runs after Basis
1 main_analyses.Rmd — none
2 prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd — none

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. The code reads files that are only inside Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip, and no script unpacks it. We unpacked it in its folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks it (such as unzip("Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip") in R), or upload the files unpacked. 1 data path was built at runtime with sprintf()/paste()/file.path() instead of written as a literal path — this is fragile authoring practice (it silently breaks if the code is run from a different working directory than the author’s own). We resolved all of these on a best-effort basis.

Execution

The code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 2 scripts: 1 ran without error, 1 errored, 0 timed out, 0 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions. A script looked for a file in another folder than the deposit has it, so before running it once more we copied it there: Jeremie-Beucler/Jeremie-Beucler-Rythm-of-thought-3e2b76b/Output/scored_chunks.csv to Output/scored_chunks.csv for main_analyses.Rmd. Building paths from the top of the project (as with here::here()), or keeping the folders the code expects, solves this.

>   ci_col  <- intersect(c("CI", "ci", "SE", "se", "se.fit"), names(pred_df))[1]
> 
>   if (is.na(fit_col)) {
>     stop("No fitted-value column found in the itsadug output.")
>   }
> 
>   out <- pred_df %>%
>     rename(.fitted = all_of(fit_col))
> 
>   if (!is.na(ci_col)) {
>     out <- out %>%
>       mutate(.lower_ci = .fitted - .data[[ci_col]],
>              .upper_ci = .fitted + .data[[ci_col]])
>   }
> 
>   if (!is.null(keep)) {
>     out <- out %>%
>       select(any_of(c(xvar, keep, ".fitted", ".lower_ci", ".upper_ci")))
>   }
> 
>   out
> }
> get_itsadug_curve <- function(model, cond, keep = NULL,
>                               xvar = "norm_mid",
>                               transform_fun = plogis) {
>   pred_raw <- get_predictions(model,
>                               cond          = cond,
>                               rm.ranef      = TRUE,
>                               sim.ci        = TRUE,
>                               print.summary = FALSE)
> 
>   pred_df <- tidy_itsadug_predictions(pred_raw, xvar = xvar, keep = keep)
> 
>   pred_df %>%
>     mutate(.fitted   = transform_fun(.fitted),
>            .lower_ci = transform_fun(.lower_ci),
>            .upper_ci = transform_fun(.upper_ci))
> }
> get_sig_segments <- function(diff_df) {
>   global_y_min <- min(diff_df$difference - diff_df$CI)
>   global_y_max <- max(diff_df$difference + diff_df$CI)
>   global_y_sig <- global_y_min - 0.1 * (global_y_max - global_y_min)
> 
>   diff_df %>%
>     mutate(sig = (difference - CI) > 0 | (difference + CI) < 0) %>%
>     group_by(deliberation_function) %>%
>     mutate(block = cumsum(sig != lag(sig, default = first(sig)))) %>%
>     ungroup() %>%
>     filter(sig) %>%
>     group_by(deliberation_function, block) %>%
>     summarise(x    = min(norm_mid),
>               xend = max(norm_mid),
>               .groups = "drop") %>%
>     mutate(y_sig = global_y_sig)
> }
> tbl_gam <- function(
>   model, caption = NULL, exponentiate = FALSE, var_labels = NULL,
>   level_labels = NULL, digits = 2, pvalue_digits = 3, fit_stats = TRUE,
>   show_formula = FALSE, section_headers = TRUE, estimate_label = NULL,
>   output = c("flextable", "data"), additional_effects = NULL
> ) {
>   stopifnot(inherits(model, "gam"))
>   output <- match.arg(output)
>   fam <- stats::family(model)
>   smry <- summary(model) # One summary, including mgcv's special RE tests.
>   if (identical(exponentiate, "auto"))
>     exponentiate <- identical(fam$family, "binomial") && identical(fam$link, "logit")
>   stopifnot(is.logical(exponentiate), length(exponentiate) == 1L)
>   if (is.null(estimate_label)) estimate_label <- if (exponentiate) "OR" else "b"
>   vl <- c(score_01 = "Score", active = "Activation", confidence_01 = "Confidence",
>           response_confidence = "Confidence", deliberation_function = "Function",
>           response = "Accuracy", subject_id = "Participant", question = "Item",
>           trial_id = "Trial", chunk_id = "Chunk", norm_mid = "Relative time",
>           log_n_chunks = "Log number of chunks",
>           lag_conf_chunk_dev_1 = "Previous confidence (within trial)",
>           lag_conf_chunk_dev_2 = "Confidence two chunks earlier (within trial)",
>           conf_trial_dev = "Confidence (trial deviation)",
>           conf_subject_mean = "Confidence (participant mean)",
>           lag_active_1 = "Previous activation", lag_active_2 = "Activation two chunks earlier",
>           lag_score_01_1 = "Previous intensity", lag_score_01_2 = "Intensity two chunks earlier",
>           lag_confidence_1 = "Previous confidence", lag_confidence_2 = "Confidence two chunks earlier",
>           lag_confidence_1_z = "Previous confidence (standardized)",
>           lag_confidence_2_z = "Confidence two chunks earlier (standardized)")
>   for (f in c("control", "generation", "justification", "regulation")) {
>     label <- tools::toTitleCase(f)
>     vl[paste0("lag_", f, "_chunk_dev_1")] <- paste0("Previous ", f, " (within trial)")
>     vl[paste0("lag_", f, "_chunk_dev_2")] <- paste0(label, " two chunks earlier (within trial)")
>     vl[paste0(f, "_trial_dev")] <- paste0(label, " (trial deviation)")
>     vl[paste0(f, "_subject_mean")] <- paste0(label, " (participant mean)")
>     for (lag in 1:2) vl[paste0("lag_",f,"_",lag)] <- paste0("Previous ",f," (n−",lag,")")
>   }
>   if (length(var_labels)) vl[names(var_labels)] <- gsub("Prior", "Previous", unname(var_labels), fixed=TRUE)
>   pv <- function(v) if (v %in% names(vl)) unname(vl[v]) else v
>   pl <- function(v,l) {
>     if (!is.null(level_labels[[v]]) && l %in% names(level_labels[[v]]))
>       return(unname(level_labels[[v]][l]))
>     if (v == "response" && l == "Incorrect") return("Biased")
>     l
>   }
>   xl <- model$xlevels
>   # Reference labels are valid only for treatment-coded fixed factors.
>   treatment <- names(xl)[vapply(names(xl),function(v) {
>     ct <- model$contrasts[[v]]
>     is.character(ct) && identical(ct,"contr.treatment")
>   }, logical(1))]
>   refs <- setNames(vapply(treatment, function(v) pl(v,xl[[v]][1]),character(1)),treatment)
>   split_factor <- function(term) {
>     for (v in names(xl)[order(-nchar(names(xl)))]) {
>       if (startsWith(term,v)) {
>         l <- substring(term,nchar(v)+1)
>         if (l %in% xl[[v]]) return(list(var=v,level=l))
>       }
>     }
>     list(var=term,level=NA_character_)
>   }
>   pp <- function(term) {
>     if (term == "(Intercept)") return("Intercept")
>     parts <- strsplit(term,":",fixed=TRUE)[[1]]
>     labs <- vapply(parts,function(part) {
>       z <- split_factor(part)
>       if (is.na(z$level)) return(pv(z$var))
>       if (!(z$var %in% treatment)) return(paste(pv(z$var),pl(z$var,z$level)))
>       if (length(parts)>1 && z$var == "deliberation_function") return(pl(z$var,z$level))
>       if (z$var == "deliberation_function") return(paste0(pl(z$var,z$level)," vs. ",refs[z$var]))
>       if (z$var == "lag_active_1") return("Previous activation (active vs. inactive)")
>       paste0(pl(z$var,z$level)," vs. ",refs[z$var])
>     },character(1))
>     paste(labs,collapse=" × ")
>   }
>   smooth_by_label <- setNames(model$smooth,vapply(model$smooth,`[[`,character(1),"label"))
>   ps <- function(term) {
>     sm <- smooth_by_label[[term]]
>     if (inherits(sm,"random.effect")) {
>       vars <- sm$term
>       fac <- vapply(vars,function(v) is.factor(model$model[[v]]),logical(1))
>       if (all(fac)) return(paste0("Random intercept: ",paste(vapply(vars,pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")))
>       return(paste0("Random slope: ",paste(vapply(vars[!fac],pv,character(1)),collapse=" × "),
>                     " by ",paste(vapply(vars[fac],pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")))
>     }
>     base <- paste(vapply(sm$term,pv,character(1)),collapse=" × ")
>     if (identical(sm$by,"NA")) return(base)
>     v <- sm$by; lev <- sm$by.level
>     if (startsWith(v,"interaction(")) {
>       vars <- trimws(strsplit(sub("^interaction\\((.*)\\)$","\\1",v),",",fixed=TRUE)[[1]])
>       # Construct full level combinations; do not split levels at periods.
>       combos <- expand.grid(lapply(vars,function(x) levels(model$model[[x]])),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
>       k <- match(lev,apply(combos,1,paste,collapse="."))
>       if (!is.na(k)) lev <- paste(mapply(pl,vars,as.character(combos[k,]),USE.NAMES=FALSE),collapse=" × ")
>     } else lev <- pl(v,lev)
>     paste0(base,": ",lev)
>   }
>   pt <- as.data.frame(smry$p.table)
>   stat_type <- if (grepl("^t",names(pt)[3])) "t" else "z"
>   critical <- if (stat_type == "t") stats::qt(.975,smry$residual.df) else stats::qnorm(.975)
>   param <- data.frame(term=rownames(pt),label=vapply(rownames(pt),pp,character(1)),
>                       estimate=pt[[1]],SE=pt[[2]],low=pt[[1]]-critical*pt[[2]],
>                       high=pt[[1]]+critical*pt[[2]],statistic=pt[[3]],p=pt[[4]],
>                       statistic_type=stat_type,row.names=NULL)
>   st <- as.data.frame(smry$s.table)
>   smooth <- data.frame(term=rownames(st),label=vapply(rownames(st),ps,character(1)),
>                        edf=st[[1]],ref_df=st[[2]],statistic=st[[3]],p=st[[4]],
>                        statistic_type=names(st)[3],row.names=NULL)
>   smooth$random <- vapply(smooth$term,function(t) inherits(smooth_by_label[[t]],"random.effect"),logical(1))
>   mm <- model$model
>   fit <- c("Model rows"=nrow(mm))
>   if (all(c("subject_id","question","norm_mid") %in% names(mm)))
>     fit["Chunks"] <- nrow(unique(mm[c("subject_id","question","norm_mid")]))
>   for (v in intersect(c("subject_id","question"),names(mm)))
>     fit[paste0(pv(v),"s")] <- length(unique(mm[[v]]))
>   if (all(c("subject_id","question") %in% names(mm))) fit["Trials"] <- nrow(unique(mm[c("subject_id","question")]))
>   fit <- c(fit,"Deviance explained (%)"=smry$dev.expl*100)
>   if (grepl("^Beta",fam$family) && is.function(fam$getTheta)) fit["Beta precision"] <- fam$getTheta(TRUE)
>   meta <- list(family=fam$family,link=fam$link,method=model$method,refs=refs,
>                formula=paste(deparse(stats::formula(model),width.cutoff=500),collapse=" "),
>                parametric_statistic=stat_type,smooth_statistic=names(st)[3],
>                residual_df=smry$residual.df,exponentiate=exponentiate,
>                fit=fit,ci_distribution=if(stat_type=="t") "t" else "normal")
>   result <- list(parametric=param,smooth=smooth,meta=meta,additional_effects=additional_effects)
>   if (output == "data") return(result)
>   format_gam_table(result, caption=caption, digits=digits, pvalue_digits=pvalue_digits,
>                    fit_stats=fit_stats, show_formula=show_formula,
>                    section_headers=section_headers, estimate_label=estimate_label)
> }
> format_gam_table <- function(result, caption=NULL, digits=2, pvalue_digits=3,
>                              fit_stats=TRUE, show_formula=FALSE,
>                              section_headers=TRUE, estimate_label=NULL) {
>   param <- result$parametric; smooth <- result$smooth; meta <- result$meta
>   exponentiate <- meta$exponentiate
>   if(is.null(estimate_label)) estimate_label <- if(exponentiate) "OR" else "b"
>   fmt <- function(x) {
>     x[abs(x)<0.5*10^(-digits)] <- 0
>     formatC(x,format="f",digits=digits)
>   }
>   fp <- function(x) vapply(x,function(p) {
>     if(is.na(p)) return("")
>     if(p<.001) return("< .001")
>     sub("^0\\.",".",formatC(p,format="f",digits=pvalue_digits))
>   },character(1))
>   test <- function(type,x) paste(if(type=="Chi.sq") "χ²" else type, "=", fmt(x))
>   keys <- c("Term","b","SE","CI","edf","ref_df","Test","p")
>   rows <- list(); kinds <- character()
>   add <- function(x,kind="value") {
>     rows[[length(rows)+1L]] <<- setNames(as.character(x),keys)
>     kinds <<- c(kinds,kind)
>   }
>   group <- function(label) if(section_headers) add(c(label,rep("",7)),"section")
>   group("Parametric coefficients")
>   est <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$estimate) else param$estimate
>   lo <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$low) else param$low
>   hi <- if(exponentiate) exp(param$high) else param$high
>   for(i in seq_len(nrow(param))) add(c(param$label[i],fmt(est[i]),fmt(param$SE[i]),
>     paste0("[",fmt(lo[i]),", ",fmt(hi[i]),"]"),"","",
>     test(param$statistic_type[i],param$statistic[i]),fp(param$p[i])))
>   for(re in c(FALSE,TRUE)) {
>     z <- smooth[smooth$random==re,,drop=FALSE]
>     if(!nrow(z)) next
>     group(if(re) "Random effects" else "Smooth terms")
>     for(i in seq_len(nrow(z))) add(c(z$label[i],"","","",fmt(z$edf[i]),fmt(z$ref_df[i]),
>       test(z$statistic_type[i],z$statistic[i]),fp(z$p[i])))
>   }
>   panel_rows <- list()
>   for(panel in result$additional_effects) {
>     start <- length(rows)+1L
>     group(panel$title)
>     z <- panel$data
>     for(i in seq_len(nrow(z))) add(c(z$label[i],fmt(z$estimate[i]),fmt(z$SE[i]),
>       paste0("[",fmt(z$low[i]),", ",fmt(z$high[i]),"]"),"","",
>       test(z$statistic_type[i],z$statistic[i]),fp(z$p_adjusted[i])))
>     panel_rows[[length(panel_rows)+1L]] <- start:(length(rows)-1L)
>   }
>   if(fit_stats) {
>     group("Sample and model fit")
>     f <- meta$fit
>     count <- function(name) formatC(f[name],format="d",big.mark=",")
>     sample <- paste0("N = ",count("Chunks")," chunks",
>       if(f["Model rows"]!=f["Chunks"]) paste0(" (",count("Model rows")," observations)") else "",
>       "; ",count("Trials")," trials; ",count("Participants")," participants; ",count("Items")," items.")
>     add(c(sample,rep("",7)),"fit")
>     add(c(paste0("Deviance explained = ",formatC(f["Deviance explained (%)"],format="f",digits=1),"%."),rep("",7)),"fit")
>   }
>   display <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind,rows),stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
>   ft <- flextable::flextable(display,col_keys=keys)
>   ft <- flextable::set_header_labels(ft,Term="Term",b=estimate_label,
>     SE=if(exponentiate) "SE (link)" else "SE",CI="95% CI",edf="edf",ref_df="Ref. df",Test="Statistic",p="p")
>   ft <- flextable::border_remove(ft)
>   ft <- flextable::font(ft,fontname="Times New Roman",part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::fontsize(ft,size=9.5,part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::padding(ft,padding=2,part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::height_all(ft,height=15/72,part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::align(ft,j=1,align="left",part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::align(ft,j=2:8,align="center",part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::valign(ft,valign="center",part="all")
>   ft <- flextable::width(ft,j=keys,width=c(2.13,.42,.42,1.04,.52,.52,.75,.50))
>   ft <- flextable::italic(ft,j=c("b","SE","edf","p"),part="header")
>   for(i in which(kinds=="section")) {
>     ft <- flextable::merge_at(ft,i=i,j=1:8,part="body")
>     ft <- flextable::bold(ft,i=i,part="body")
>   }
>   for(i in which(kinds=="fit")) {
>     ft <- flextable::merge_at(ft,i=i,j=1:8,part="body")
>     ft <- flextable::align(ft,i=i,j=1,align="left",part="body")
>   }
>   rule <- officer::fp_border(color="black",width=.75)
>   ft <- flextable::hline_top(ft,border=rule,part="header")
>   ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft,border=rule,part="header")
>   ft <- flextable::hline_bottom(ft,border=rule,part="body")
>   ft <- flextable::set_table_properties(ft,layout="fixed",opts_word=list(split=FALSE,keep_with_next=FALSE))
>   ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=which(kinds=="section"),value=TRUE,part="body")
>   for(i in panel_rows) ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=i,value=TRUE,part="body")
>   # Keep random effects and the short summary panels together on long tables.
>   tail_start <- which(kinds=="section" & display$Term=="Random effects")
>   if(length(tail_start) && nrow(display)>tail_start)
>     ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=tail_start:(nrow(display)-1L),value=TRUE,part="body")
>   # Keep the small sample-summary block on one page.
>   frows <- which(kinds=="fit")
>   if(length(frows)>1) ft <- flextable::keep_with_next(ft,i=head(frows,-1),value=TRUE,part="body")
>   if(show_formula) ft <- flextable::add_footer_lines(ft,values=meta$formula)
>   if(!is.null(caption)) ft <- flextable::set_caption(ft,caption)
>   attr(ft,"gamm_report") <- result
>   attr(ft,"gamm_row_kinds") <- kinds
>   ft
> }

> check_autocorr <- function(model, series_vars,
>                            max_lag = 4,
>                            problematic_threshold = 0.2) {
>   model_name <- deparse(substitute(model))
> 
>   mdf <- as.data.frame(model$model)
>   mdf$.resid <- residuals(model)
>   mdf$.sid   <- interaction(mdf[, series_vars, drop = FALSE], drop = TRUE)
> 
>   # total series and how many are long enough to contribute a lag-1 pair
>   series_lengths <- mdf %>% count(.sid, name = "len")
>   n_series_total <- nrow(series_lengths)
>   n_series_used  <- sum(series_lengths$len >= 2)
> 
>   # pooled: insert NAs between series, then one acf() over the lot
>   pooled <- mdf %>%
>     arrange(.sid) %>%
>     group_by(.sid) %>%
>     group_modify(~ tibble(r = c(.x$.resid, NA_real_))) %>%
>     ungroup() %>%
>     pull(r)
> 
>   acf_pooled <- stats::acf(pooled, lag.max = max_lag,
>                            plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass)
>   lag1_pooled <- acf_pooled$acf[2, 1, 1]
> 
>   tibble(
>     model          = model_name,
>     n_series       = n_series_total,
>     n_series_used  = n_series_used,
>     lag1_pooled    = lag1_pooled,
>     problematic    = abs(lag1_pooled) > problematic_threshold
>   )
> }

>   group_by(subject_id, question) %>%

>   # recalculate norm_mid etc. on the remaining chunks
>   mutate(
>     question_start    = min(start_time, na.rm = TRUE),
>     question_end      = max(end_time,   na.rm = TRUE),
>     question_duration = question_end - question_start,
>     norm_start        = (start_time - question_start) / question_duration,
>     norm_end          = (end_time   - question_start) / question_duration,
>     norm_mid          = ((start_time + end_time) / 2 - question_start) / question_duration
>   ) %>%
>   ungroup() %>% 
>   # we add the log n chunks as a control variable in our models
>   group_by(subject_id, question) %>%
>   mutate(n_chunks = n_distinct(chunk_id)) %>%
>   ungroup() %>%
>   mutate(log_n_chunks = log(n_chunks))

> exclusion_by_response <- function(from_df, kept_df, pass_label) {
>   from_trials <- from_df %>% distinct(subject_id, question, response)
>   kept_keys   <- kept_df %>% distinct(subject_id, question)
> 
>   total_by_resp <- from_trials %>% count(response, name = "n_trials")
>   excluded_by_resp <- from_trials %>%
>     anti_join(kept_keys, by = c("subject_id", "question")) %>%
>     count(response, name = "n_excluded")
> 
>   total_by_resp %>%
>     left_join(excluded_by_resp, by = "response") %>%
>     mutate(
>       n_excluded   = tidyr::replace_na(n_excluded, 0L),

>       pass         = pass_label
>     ) %>%
>     select(pass, response, n_trials, n_excluded, pct_excluded)
> }

> apa_corr_label <- function(rho, p) {
>   rho_str <- sprintf("%.2f", abs(rho))
>   rho_str <- sub("^0", "", rho_str)
> 
>   if (rho < 0) {
>     rho_str <- paste0("-", rho_str)
>   }
> 
>   if (p < .001) {
>     p_str <- "italic(p) < .001"
>   } else {
>     p_formatted <- sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p))
>     p_str <- sprintf("italic(p) == '%s'", p_formatted)
>   }
> 
>   sprintf("italic(rho) == '%s' * ',' ~ %s", rho_str, p_str)
> }

> cor_with_ci <- function(x, y, conf_level = 0.95, n_boot = 2000, seed = 123) {
>   df <- tibble(x = x, y = y) %>% drop_na()
>   r <- cor(df$x, df$y, method = "spearman")
>   set.seed(seed)
>   boot_r <- replicate(n_boot, {
>     idx <- sample.int(nrow(df), replace = TRUE)
>     cor(df$x[idx], df$y[idx], method = "spearman")
>   })
>   alpha <- (1 - conf_level) / 2
>   tibble(r = unname(r),
>          conf_low = quantile(boot_r, alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
>          conf_high = quantile(boot_r, 1 - alpha, na.rm = TRUE),
>          n = nrow(df))
> }
> cor_sum_spearman <- cor_long_all %>%
>   group_by(Measure, Experiment) %>%
>   summarise(tmp = list(cor_with_ci(human_avg, llm_raw)),
>             .groups = "drop") %>%
>   unnest(tmp)

> cor_mat_long <- function(df_wide, vars, panel_label) {
>   dat <- df_wide %>% select(all_of(vars)) %>% drop_na()
>   idx_tbl <- tibble(var = vars, idx = seq_along(vars))
> 
>   crossing(var1 = vars, var2 = vars) %>%
>     mutate(
>       r = map2_dbl(var1, var2, ~ cor(dat[[.x]], dat[[.y]])),
>       p = map2_dbl(var1, var2,
>                    ~ suppressWarnings(cor.test(dat[[.x]], dat[[.y]])$p.value)),
>       stars = star_p(p),
>       panel = panel_label
>     ) %>%
>     left_join(idx_tbl, by = c("var1" = "var")) %>% rename(i = idx) %>%
>     left_join(idx_tbl, by = c("var2" = "var")) %>% rename(j = idx) %>%
>     mutate(across(c(r, p), ~ if_else(j > i, NA_real_, .x)),
>            stars = if_else(j > i, NA_character_, stars)) %>%
>     select(panel, var1, var2, r, p, stars) %>%
>     mutate(var1 = factor(var1, levels = vars),
>            var2 = factor(var2, levels = vars),
>            label = if_else(is.na(r), "",
>                            paste0(sprintf("%.2f", r), stars)))
> }

Duplicate files across repo mirrors

2 files are byte-identical to another file already in the run (the paper links more than one repository/component that mirrors the same materials). They were only run once, from its first occurrence, to avoid wasted duplicate execution: main_analyses.Rmd at Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip/Jeremie-Beucler-Rythm-of-thought-3e2b76b/Analyses/main_analyses.Rmd (same as main_analyses.Rmd at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought/main/Analyses/main_analyses.Rmd); prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd at Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip/Jeremie-Beucler-Rythm-of-thought-3e2b76b/Analyses/prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd (same as prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd at https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought/main/Analyses/prompt_optimization_analysis.rmd).

Python code

This module also assesses whether the paper’s Python code could be run on its data, and — because execute = TRUE — actually ran it. We examined 4 Python code files.

Run order

The scripts were ordered by their data dependencies (a script writing a file another reads runs first) and numeric filename prefixes. Python has no source()-equivalent import-based ordering signal (an import loads a module, not the paper’s own analysis flow), so that basis never applies here.

Order File Runs after Basis
1 open_ended_labeling.ipynb — none
2 prompt_optimization_LLM_calls.ipynb — none
3 speech_to_text_conversion.ipynb — none
4 chunking_and_scoring_LLM_calls.ipynb speech_to_text_conversion.ipynb dependency

File paths

Every data path in the code works in the repository as deposited. The code reads files that are only inside Jeremie-Beucler/Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip, and no script unpacks it. We unpacked it in its folder before the run. So that others can run the code as deposited, start the code with a line that unpacks it (such as zipfile.ZipFile("Rythm-of-thought-v1.1.0.zip").extractall() in Python), or upload the files unpacked.

Execution

The Python code was run. Each script ran in an isolated Docker container against a throwaway copy of the repository, in the run order above, with a 300-second per-script timeout. Of 4 scripts: 1 ran without error, 0 errored, 2 timed out, 1 could not run because one of its own dependencies is unavailable, 0 did not parse, and 0 are written for Python 2 and not run. Running against current package versions: a break can reflect version drift, which argues for pinning versions (e.g. in a requirements.txt). A script looked for a file in another folder than the deposit has it, so before running it once more we copied it there: Jeremie-Beucler/Jeremie-Beucler-Rythm-of-thought-3e2b76b/Data/data_long.csv to Data/data_long.csv for chunking_and_scoring_LLM_calls.ipynb. Building paths from the top of the project (as with here::here()), or keeping the folders the code expects, solves this.

Dependency-unavailable errors

1 script could not run because its own dependency is unavailable — the package failed to pip install. This is an infrastructure limitation, not a defect in the paper’s code, so it does not force the traffic light red.

File
speech_to_text_conversion.ipynb

os.chdir() in the code

4 scripts call os.chdir(). This is bad practice: it hardcodes where the code must run (often an absolute path on the author’s own machine) and breaks the moment the code is run anywhere else. To run the code we replaced these calls with pass. Any such script that then ran is reproducible only after ignoring an os.chdir() that should not have been in the code and needs to be fixed.

Reproducible after removing os.chdir(): open_ended_labeling.ipynb.

All code and output

Reported vs. reproduced

161 statistical tests reported in the manuscript text were checked against the extracted analysis output: 1 matched (1 fully, 0 partially) — 0.6% found.

Some reported values were only found alongside OTHER components after being separated from their own originally-reported neighbours (e.g. a mean split from its own confidence interval). The “Plausible” column marks whether that split is well-supported: TRUE when the pieces still trace back to the same underlying variable (via the output’s own row labels), FALSE when no such link was found — a FALSE match is not necessarily wrong, but is worth checking against its own Source file/Analysis columns before treating it as confirmed.

Self-reproducible output (JASP / jamovi / SPSS Viewer / Jupyter notebook)

8 JASP/jamovi/SPSS-Viewer/notebook files bundle the analyses and their saved results together, so the reported statistics are recoverable from the files itself, with nothing re-run. We extracted 342 result tables (4 individual statistics), typed with the STATO ontology, and export them as a statistical-output JSON document (in the logs) and as queryable rows.

More detail

Ethics Approval Check

The paper does not appear to report data about individual people or animals (we found: simulations; figures about groups or things), so we do not expect an ethics statement.

We based this on:

Fitted trajectories are reported with random effects set to zero (i.e., for an average participant and item), so that curves reflect population-level trajectories.

Together, these results reveal a clear population-level temporal structure in participants’ verbalized reasoning.

Overall, we found a clear population-level temporal organization of deliberation: generation was frequently engaged from the beginning, whereas justification, control, and regulation became increasingly recruited as reasoning progressed.

Ethics statement:

The original data were collected under a protocol approved by the Office for Human Subjects Protection at Florida State University (STUDY00000697), and all participants gave informed consent in the original study. reasoning effort from none (“GPT -no forced-zero rule”) through low, medium, and high (“GPT -low reasoning,” “GPT -medium reasoning,” and “GPT -high reasoning”).

Power Analysis Check

No power analyses were detected.

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen’s d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.
